questions.question: When loading cargo, it is important to:

options.text: Stack items as high as possible.
Know the weight capacity of the suspension system.
Put light items under heavier items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know the weight capacity of the suspension system.
questions.explanation: It is your job as a driver to make sure your vehicle is not overloaded. You must know the legal weight limits and the maximum weight your vehicle can safely carry, including the suspension system's weight limit.

questions.question: Most heavy vehicles use the ____ method when changing gears.
questions.explanation: Most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions that do not have synchronized gears require double clutching to change gears safely.

questions.question: A truck should be parked:

options.text: So that it must be backed up to leave.
So that it can be pulled forward to leave.

questions.correctAnswerText: So that it can be pulled forward to leave.
questions.explanation: Backing is always dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Avoid backing whenever possible. Choose parking spaces where you can pull forward when you leave.

questions.question: If you're not sure how to put out a fire in your vehicle, you should:
questions.explanation: If you do not know what type of fire extinguisher to use on a vehicle fire, especially if hazardous materials are involved, wait for firefighters to arrive and let them put out the fire.

questions.question: Air brake leakage for a single vehicle should not be more than ____ in one minute during a static leakage test.
questions.explanation: During a static leakage test, a single vehicle's air brakes should lose no more than 2 psi per minute. If air leaks faster than this, do not drive the vehicle—it needs repair.

questions.question: If you cause a death by negligently operating a CMV, you will lose your CDL for at least:
questions.explanation: A first conviction for causing a death through negligent operation of a CMV means you will lose your CDL for at least one year.

questions.question: An Individual Vehicle Distance Record (IVDR) does not need to include which of the following?
questions.explanation: An IVDR must show the distance traveled and fuel purchased. It must include trip dates and total distance. It does not need to show how many vehicles were passed.

questions.question: Air tank drains should:

options.text: Not be used by the driver.
Only be used when it rains.
Be used to drain the tanks completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used to drain the tanks completely.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in brake systems contains water and oil. This buildup can damage the brakes. You must open air tank drains manually every day to remove water and oil.

questions.question: ____ are most affected by strong winds.
questions.explanation: Strong winds make it hard to control your vehicle. This problem is worse for drivers of lighter commercial vehicles.

questions.question: When should you slow down for a curve?
questions.explanation: Always slow to a safe speed before you enter a curve. Slowing down while in the curve can cause you to skid.

questions.question: Which is NOT a recommended way to spot vehicle problems?

options.text: Checking critical items only at the start and end of a trip

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking critical items only at the start and end of a trip
questions.explanation: Check your vehicle regularly during a trip. Look at the instrument panel and gauges. Check your mirrors, tires, cargo, and lights. Use all your senses and watch for early signs of trouble.

questions.question: Dry bulk tanks:

options.text: Are usually not allowed to cross railroad tracks.

questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks need special care. They have high centers of gravity and the cargo weight can shift while you drive.

questions.question: What is the best advice for driving in fog?
questions.explanation: Driving in fog is always dangerous. Avoid it if possible. If you must drive in fog, turn on your low beam headlights and fog lights, even during the day.

questions.question: When using a mirror, you should:

options.text: Stare at the mirror for a long time.
Use only the driver's side mirror.

questions.explanation: Look at mirrors quickly. If you stare too long, you may travel far down the road without seeing what is ahead.

questions.question: Texting while driving should:
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is dangerous and distracting. It is not allowed at any time when driving a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: Traction is important for:
questions.explanation: You cannot brake or steer without good traction. Make sure your tires are in good condition before you start driving.

questions.question: If your brakes fail going downhill, your best option to stop is:

options.text: Let the vehicle drift to a stop.

questions.explanation: If your brakes fail on a downhill, look for a way to stop outside your vehicle. An escape ramp is the safest option.

questions.question: If you see a distracted driver ahead, you should:

options.text: Stay at a safe distance from the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay at a safe distance from the vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you see a distracted driver, give them plenty of space. Keep a safe following distance.

questions.question: If there is a fire in your vehicle and you do not know how to put it out, you should:

options.text: Try to spray the flames with water.
Move away and wait for firefighters.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move away and wait for firefighters.
questions.explanation: If you are not sure how to put out a fire, do not try. Move away from the flames and let firefighters handle it. This is especially important for hazardous materials fires.

questions.question: Within 10 minutes of stopping on the road, you must:
questions.explanation: If you stop on the side of the road, you must place emergency warning devices within 10 minutes.

questions.question: If you meet an aggressive driver, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your vehicle in front of them.

questions.explanation: Do not react to an aggressive driver's actions or angry gestures. Do not make eye contact, as this may provoke them. Move out of their way if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: How should you do an offset back/left parking maneuver?

options.text: Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
Drive straight back, then pull forward to the left.
Pull straight forward, then drive straight back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/left parking maneuver, first pull straight forward. Then back up to the left. Your vehicle must stay within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, what can a separate air tank do?

options.text: Make the air brakes work more effectively.
Charge the brakes on the rear trailer.

questions.explanation: A separate air tank can temporarily release the spring brakes if they have been activated due to low air pressure. This allows the driver to move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?
questions.explanation: When driving in fog, reduce your speed. Fog makes it harder to see, so driving slower helps you stay safe.

questions.question: How often must drivers check that cargo is secure?
questions.explanation: Check cargo securement before starting, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles after that.

questions.question: What can help you avoid being an aggressive driver?

options.text: Give other drivers the benefit of the doubt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give other drivers the benefit of the doubt.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, assume other drivers have good reasons for what they do. Do not take their actions personally.

questions.question: When backing up with a trailer, how do you follow its turn?

options.text: Do nothing. The vehicle will naturally follow the trailer.
Change the direction of the steering wheel.
Turn the steering wheel even harder in the same direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change the direction of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, first turn the steering wheel opposite to your desired direction. Once the trailer starts to turn, reverse the steering wheel direction to follow the trailer.

questions.question: What should you do when driving?

options.text: Use turn signals only when other vehicles are nearby.
Do not use turn signals in construction zones.
Always use turn signals to tell others your intentions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use turn signals to tell others your intentions.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. This warns other drivers about your actions, even if no one is near you.

questions.question: What can happen if you do not drain air tanks?

options.text: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
Too much air collects in the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air tanks must be drained regularly to remove water and oil. If water remains in the tanks, it can freeze in cold weather and cause brake failure.

questions.question: If a load is 10 feet long, what is the minimum number of tie-downs needed?
questions.explanation: Use one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. However, always use at least two tie-downs, even for smaller loads.

questions.question: When turning, what should you do?

options.text: Turn off your signal just before you turn.
Signal only if there are vehicles in front of you.

questions.explanation: Turn on your signal well before you turn or change lanes. Keep the signal on while you turn. Turn it off after the turn is complete if your vehicle does not turn it off automatically.

questions.question: Can you use radial and bias-ply tires together?

options.text: Yes, you can use them together.
Yes, you can use them together on the front of the vehicle.
No, you should not use them together.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, you should not use them together.
questions.explanation: Do not mix radial and bias-ply tires. All tires on a vehicle must be the same type and size.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Only rely on warning signals to tell you if a train is coming.
Only rely on what other drivers do to tell you if a train is coming.
Do not rely only on warning signals to tell you if a train is coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not rely only on warning signals to tell you if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Do not depend only on warning signals, gates, or flaggers to warn you about trains. Watch carefully at crossings without gates or signals. Always assume a train is coming at any railroad crossing.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve in an air brake system releases air, what does this mean?

options.text: The air pressure is too high.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air pressure is too high.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air when pressure gets too high. If this happens, something is wrong with the system. Have a mechanic check it.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, what will you be asked to do?

options.text: Tell the examiner what you are checking and why.
Guess how much a load weighs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the examiner what you are checking and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must inspect your entire vehicle. You must explain what you are checking and why.

questions.question: What is a problem with retarders?

options.text: They help slow down a vehicle.

questions.explanation: A retarder slows down a vehicle and reduces brake wear. However, retarders can be loud and are not allowed in all areas.

questions.question: When you change lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Other drivers will move out of your way.
Wait to change lanes until you are in an intersection.

questions.explanation: Always change lanes slowly and smoothly. This keeps your vehicle safe and gives other drivers time to react to your movements.

questions.question: Where must placards be placed on a vehicle carrying hazardous cargo?

options.text: On the front, rear, and both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the front, rear, and both sides.
questions.explanation: Placards must be placed on the front, rear, and both sides of a vehicle carrying hazardous cargo. They must be visible from every direction.

questions.question: Is it legal to read text messages while driving?

options.text: Yes, only if you are not towing a trailer.

questions.explanation: Sending and reading text messages while driving is dangerous and against the law.

questions.question: If the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops working, what happens?

options.text: The truck will have no brakes.
The truck can only drive at low speeds.
The truck will still have brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck will still have brakes.
questions.explanation: ABS is an extra system added to regular brakes. It prevents wheels from locking up during hard braking. If ABS fails, your regular brakes will still work. You can drive and brake normally.

questions.question: When a vehicle starts, the coolant temperature should:
questions.explanation: When an engine starts, the coolant temperature should gradually increase toward the normal operating temperature.

questions.question: Which vehicle requires a CDL?
questions.explanation: A CDL is not required for military vehicles, emergency vehicles, farm equipment, or recreational vehicles. However, a CDL is required to drive a school bus.

questions.question: ____ is required emergency equipment.
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must have proper emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one fire extinguisher.

questions.question: When driving in wet conditions, no spray from other vehicles' tires means:

options.text: Ice has formed on the road.
The spray is trapped under the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ice has formed on the road.
questions.explanation: In wet conditions, no spray from other tires means ice has formed on the road. Drive carefully in wet and freezing weather.

questions.question: To prevent hydroplaning on wet roads:

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition with deep tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your tires in good condition with deep tread.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens more when tire pressure is low or tire tread is worn. If you start to hydroplane, release the accelerator and push in the clutch to slow down.

questions.question: If you see taillights while driving in fog:

options.text: The lights may not show where the road is because the vehicle may have left the roadway.
You can be sure the vehicle is on the road.
The lights may be an optical illusion.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lights may not show where the road is because the vehicle may have left the roadway.
questions.explanation: In fog, lights are not a reliable guide to where the road is. A vehicle with lights on may have pulled off the road.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: It is safe to drive on a tire missing one or two lug nuts.
A cracked lock ring is safe if you drive slower than 55 mph.
A missing clamp on a rim is dangerous and needs to be fixed.

questions.correctAnswerText: A missing clamp on a rim is dangerous and needs to be fixed.
questions.explanation: Missing clamps, spacers, studs, or lugs are dangerous. Mismatched, bent, or cracked lock rings are also unsafe. Check your tires and rims before driving a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: After changing a tire, the driver should stop shortly after to:

options.text: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
Look for rocks in the tire tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop a short distance later and recheck that the lug nuts are tight.

questions.question: When transporting cargo, check that it is secure every:
questions.explanation: Check cargo securement within the first 50 miles of a trip, then every three hours or 150 miles.

questions.question: What is traction?

options.text: Friction between the tires and road
The time it takes for brakes to work

questions.correctAnswerText: Friction between the tires and road
questions.explanation: Traction is the grip between your tires and the road. You need good traction to brake and steer safely.
